messages.subject: Re: Displaying a unique big dataset, is shiny the good solution?
parts:
See the section on renderImage on this page: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/images.html You can use this to send pre-rendered images with Shiny. Make sure to set your imageOutput's width and height to match the size of your images.

On Wed, Apr 12, 2017 at 6:45 AM Olivier <o.n...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello everyone,

I am wondering how to deal with my problematic and two solutions come to my mind. One would involve Shiny which I do not know yet. I ask here if it is appropriate to my use case.

Here is my problem:
I have a big dataset that in R that represent an object of ~500MB that I plot with ggplot2.
There is 20 millions int values to plot that are associated with a 5 level factor
I would like to set up a webapps where users could visualize this dataset, using different filter that rely on the factor to display all the data are once or for example a subset corresponding to 1 of the factor.
The problem is that when I write the plot it takes a couple of minute (~10 minutes)

Solution 1 : The best one for the user would be to use Shiny. But is there a way to have the plot already preloaded in shiny so it can be easily displayed without having to rewrite the whole plot every time?

Solution 2 : Without shiny, I would have different plots of the dataset already written on the server and I will have to rebuild a UI to let user visualizes the different pictures. If I do that I will have to restrict the possible use cases of displaying the data.

Thanks for any advises!

--
